about.headline: Crafting with technical rigor,
about.roleCategory: SOFTWARE ENGINEERING · FOCUS ON BACKEND & AI
about.quote: “I believe that great software unites logical precision and aesthetic sensibility — turning the complex into something simple and enjoyable for the user.”
bioParagraphs: I am a Software Engineering undergraduate at Pontifícia Universidade Católica de Minas Gerais (PUC Minas), passionate about the intersection between rigorous logic, systems architecture, and thoughtful interface design.

I believe building good software goes beyond writing functional code: it is about delivering pleasant, intuitive, and purpose-driven products. I cultivate a disciplined routine of continuous learning, diving deep into computer science fundamentals, object-oriented programming with Java, and the modern web ecosystem with JavaScript and React.

I operate natively with Artificial Intelligence, leveraging cutting-edge AI models and developer agents to explore novel ideas, rapidly prototype solutions, debug complex architectures, and sustain a productive engineering workflow, always applying critical judgment over code elegance and maintainability.

projects.headline: Selected projects,
projects.gvsTagline: Complete overhaul of the company digital presence and corporate portal
projects.gvsDesc: A real professional project conceived and developed entirely by me for Grupo GVS, redesigning the brand's digital image for the clean energy generation market. Features power plant architecture, careers portal, and socio-environmental initiatives.
projects.xulambisTagline: Pizzeria ordering and management system developed in Java (OOP)
projects.xulambisDesc: An academic project developed collaboratively in class at PUC Minas, simulating the backend and operational logic of a pizzeria. Built with strict Object-Oriented Programming, inventory management, dynamic ingredient calculation, and an interactive terminal CLI interface.

skills.headline: Technical repertoire,
skills.headlineHighlight: from backend to interface, with AI in the loop.
skills.subtitle: Every technology here has a real project behind it. Spin the globe and click an icon to see where I used it.
skills.hint: Drag to spin · click a technology
skills.globeLabel: Technology globe. Use Tab to move through the icons.
skills.emptyBody: The text shows up here, with an example of a project where I used it.

python.name: Python
python.about: A language with lean syntax, used from automation to data science. It is where I learned algorithms in my first semester.
python.example: Drift Invaders, the final project for Introduction to Algorithms, built by a team of four: a Pygame arcade with five waves, local co-op mode and 74 pytest tests.

java.name: Java
java.about: A mature, typed, object-oriented language behind much of enterprise software.
java.example: Xulambs Pizza, in Modular Programming: I wrote PedidoLocal inheriting from Pedido, adding a 10% service fee to the sales receipt.

spring.name: Spring Boot
spring.about: A Java framework that starts a web application with dependency injection and almost no configuration.
spring.example: In my DIAW AV1, the service loads the TSE candidates CSV (1,832 records from Minas Gerais) on startup and filters by gender, education and age, rendered with Thymeleaf.

nodejs.name: Node.js
nodejs.about: A runtime that executes JavaScript outside the browser, common in servers and build tools.
nodejs.example: I used it in the first-semester interdisciplinary project at PUC Minas.

junit.name: JUnit
junit.about: An automated testing framework for Java.
junit.example: In the Modular Programming labs I write tests in the Arrange-Act-Assert pattern, like the one that checks a sale's total in VendaDia.

rest.name: REST APIs
rest.about: A contract for systems to talk over the web: resources accessed through HTTP methods.
rest.example: This portfolio's contact form sends messages through the EmailJS API, which only accepts them with a valid reCAPTCHA token.

git.name: Git & GitHub
git.about: Code versioning and collaboration on remote repositories.
git.example: Each PUC assignment lives in its own branch (Aula2309, Aula2110), and this portfolio follows feat:, fix:, docs: commits.

html.name: HTML
html.about: The markup language that structures the content of every web page.
html.example: In Receitas de Minas, the cheese bread page uses only native HTML: a popover for the chef's secret tip and contenteditable for personal notes.

css.name: CSS
css.about: The style language that defines a page's layout, color and typography.
css.example: In the DIW-09-04 assignment I arranged geometric shapes with Flexbox, the basis of the layouts I build today.

javascript.name: JavaScript
javascript.about: The browser's programming language, which gives pages their behavior.
javascript.example: In the DIW assignments I built a movie catalog with map, filter and reduce, and a product showcase with search and category filters straight in the DOM.

react.name: React
react.about: A library for building interfaces out of reusable components.
react.example: This portfolio: React 19 with Vite, one component per section and every string in Portuguese and English through i18next.

tailwind.name: Tailwind CSS
tailwind.about: A utility-first CSS framework: styles are composed from classes right in the markup.
tailwind.example: The whole layout of this portfolio, this globe included, is built with Tailwind v4.

wordpress.name: WordPress
wordpress.about: The CMS behind much of the web, with pages assembled in visual editors such as Elementor.
wordpress.example: Grupo GVS's corporate website, live at grupogvs.com.br, was redesigned by me in WordPress with Elementor: power plants, careers and social-environmental projects.

vercel.name: Vercel
vercel.about: A front-end hosting platform with automatic deploys from Git.
vercel.example: It hosts this portfolio at victorcandido.dev: every push to main becomes a new deploy, with no manual step.

huggingface.name: Hugging Face
huggingface.about: A platform for open AI models that also hosts applications on Spaces.
huggingface.example: It hosted the website of my first-semester interdisciplinary project.

prompt.name: Prompt Engineering
prompt.about: Structuring instructions and context so language models answer precisely.
prompt.example: I use language models every day to prototype, debug and review code, always checking the output, and I record each project's decisions in an Obsidian vault.
